paper.title_en: A general-purpose trigger and tracking system for the beam tests of particle detector prototypes
paper.abstract_en: The research and development of new detectors for high-energy particle physics includes a prototyping phase followed by a validation study usually through dedicated beam-test campaigns. In this context, the characterization of a detector typically requires ancillary systems capable of providing precise triggering, synchronization, and reference tracking information. We propose a general-purpose trigger and tracking system, a flexible and portable solution designed for beam-test applications providing data readout across heterogeneous detector subsystems and accurate event reconstruction, based on commercial off-the-shelf components. The system integrates a scalable low-cost trigger and tracking (TT) setup based on scintillating fibers and SiPMs, a centralized master unit responsible for trigger generation and distribution, and a modular DAQ architecture enabling synchronous event-by-event readout of both the TT and the devices under test. A dedicated control software provides unified run control and system configuration. The proposed system is the final product of an intense R&D activity carried out by our group in recent years on scintillating fiber trackers equipped with SiPM readout. It has found applications in the beam tests of different prototypes of various detectors performed at the CERN PS and SPS facilities. In this paper, we will present, as an example, the results of a test performed on a RICH prototype at the CERN PS.
